flags.reason: The States description says “Pressed feedback is shown only while a pointer is down.” On the web, holding Enter or Space on the focused control shows it too: AutoplayControl drops to 70% opacity whenever its Pressable reports pressed (AutoplayControl.tsx line 72, 0.1.78-dbe0e02), and react-native-web 0.21.2's Pressable sets pressed from keyboard presses as well (PressResponder.js lines 236–243 start a press on an Enter or Space keydown and lines 209–213 end it on keyup; Pressable index.js lines 66 and 131). Confirmed in headless Chrome on the installed build on 29 October: on this guide, the focused live Pause control went from opacity 1 to 0.7 while Enter was held and back to 1 on release, and the same with Space. Every other sentence the guide renders still holds on dbe0e02, so the entry quotes the States card “While pressed, the control drops to 70% opacity.” and leaves the “only while a pointer is down” sentence out. Fix the sentence (for example “Pressed feedback is shown only while the control is being pressed, by pointer or by Enter or Space.”), publish, and re-extract the States section. Added by Claude Code in the overnight run agentpack-batch13, for Marcin to confirm. Guide fix #537.

placementAdvice.text: Place it on media or a dark surface: the white circle stands out, so the target is easy to find.

placementAdvice.text: The control does not stretch or shrink with its host: tokens fix its size at 36 × 36 px.

placementAdvice.text: Leave room around the 36 px circle so it is easy to press.

from.quote: Leave room around the 36 px circle so it is easy to press.

placementAdvice.text: Keep progress visible: Carousel’s Numbered type places the control beside NumberPagination, so people can see which slide is showing.

configuration.text: Show the action a press will take: pause while content plays, play while it is stopped.

from.quote: Show the action a press will take: pause while content plays, play while it is stopped.

configuration.text: state swaps the icon between pause and play. Nothing else changes: tokens fix the circle and its colors in a single mode, and the icon is always 24 px.

from.quote: state swaps the icon between pause and play. Nothing else changes: tokens fix the circle and its colors in a single mode, and the icon is always 24 px.

configuration.text: state="pause" is the default: it tells people a press will stop the slideshow, video, or audio.

from.quote: The default. It tells people a press will stop the slideshow, video, or audio.

configuration.text: state="play" is shown after playback stops; a press should start it again.

from.quote: Shown after playback stops. A press should start it again.

configuration.text: Don't show play while slides advance: the play icon suggests the slides are already stopped, so people cannot tell how to pause them.

from.quote: The play icon suggests the slides are already stopped, so people cannot tell how to pause them.

configuration.text: The control has no timer: Carousel’s Numbered type owns autoplay, with a 4-second default interval.

from.quote: The control has no timer: Carousel’s Numbered type owns autoplay, with a 4-second default interval.

configuration.text: In Carousel’s Numbered type, the Carousel owns the timer and swaps the control’s state.

rules.text: The control shows no text: its icon has to describe what a press will do, and nearby content has to show what is playing.

examples.purpose: Content advancing, such as a slideshow the screen is playing: the control offers Pause, named “Pause slideshow”, the more specific name the Sources note gives as its example. The screen owns playback: when the control is pressed it stops the slides and passes state="play". A label that is set replaces the state's own name (Pause or Play), so the screen passes a label that matches each state. The empty onPress stands for the screen's own handler.

from.quote: The default. It tells people a press will stop the slideshow, video, or audio.

examples.purpose: Content stopped: the control offers Play and, with no accessibilityLabel, is named “Play” after its state. A press should start playback again; the screen then passes state="pause". The empty onPress stands for the screen's own handler.

from.quote: Shown after playback stops. A press should start it again.

props.description: Without it, the control is named Pause or Play from state; the icon is hidden from assistive technology. Declared: Accessible name. Defaults to the action for `state` (`Pause` or `Play`).
